count_notes.creatures: 27 Dungeon Master creature types (engines/dm/group.h) plus 60 Ultima IV creature entries (conf/creatures.xml). MM1 monster table (195) not counted: its file is not in the box.
count_notes.classes: 6 MM1 classes, 10 Xeen classes, 8 Ultima IV town class NPCs, 4 DM champion schools. Overlapping concepts across engines, not merged.
count_notes.weapons: 16 Ultima IV weapon entries plus 5 DM weapon class bands.
count_notes.gear_sets: 8 Ultima IV armour tiers plus 5 DM armour types.
count_notes.zones: 9 Ultima IV map kinds (world, city, combat, dungeon, shrine, castle, town, village, ruins) plus 7 DM square types.

creature_families: DM creature types: 27 (ids 0-26): insect and vermin, slimes and rats, eyes, golems and rockpiles, undead, animated armour, elementals, demons, red dragon, three lord types (engines/dm/group.h lines 41-67)

Ultima IV creature table: 60 entries: 2 horse entries, town class NPCs (8), town creatures (8), water creatures (5), forces of nature (2, passive: wontattack, 255 HP), main creatures (28), non-standard entries (7) (conf/creatures.xml lines 12-80)
Ultima IV attributes: encounterSize (35 entries), leader (27), ranged (21), resists (10), movement (10), ambushes (8), swims (6), flies (5), undead (4), nochest (4), divides (at least 2)
MM1 monster table: 195 entries, loaded from monsters.txt (not in box); loader engines/mm/mm1/data/monsters.cpp line 49

top_creatures.label: Splitting slime swarm
top_creatures.why: Encounter of 15 with ambushes and a split-on-hit flag; reads as a moving crowd at 375 wide.
top_creatures.keep: Split on hit; ambush from a tile.
top_creatures.change: Our split rule (not a copy), our crowd shape and sound.

top_creatures.label: Fire-field phantom
top_creatures.why: Splits, has a leader, moves onto other creatures and the party, resists fire, fires a random ranged tile.
top_creatures.keep: A hazard body that walks across other bodies.
top_creatures.change: Our fire look and our leader rule.

top_creatures.label: Leader-bound undead band
top_creatures.why: Undead, leader-bound, ambushes, resists sleep: a band that reads as one threat.
top_creatures.keep: Leader-follower band with an undead tag.
top_creatures.change: Our band size and resist type.

top_creatures.label: Four-flyer ranged encounter
top_creatures.why: Flies, ranged, encounter size 4: a many-vs-one test in the air.
top_creatures.keep: Small flying group with ranged attacks.

top_creatures.label: Walking armour
top_creatures.why: A whole armour set as a creature: one silhouette that reads as a knight.

top_creatures.label: Floating eye
top_creatures.why: A flyer type that reads as its own family at 375 wide.
top_creatures.change: Our eye art and our attack.

top_creatures.label: Three-lord top tier
top_creatures.why: Three lord types at the end of the list suggest a top tier with a shared visual language.

top_creatures.label: Stone golem
top_creatures.why: A heavy slow body with the classic golem silhouette, readable at distance.

weapon_families: DM weapon class bands: swing (0); throw (dagger and axes 2; bow ammunition 10; sling ammunition 11; poison dart 12); shoot bow (16-31); shoot sling (32-47); magic and special (112 upward) (engines/dm/dungeonman.h lines 84-100)

gear_tiers: Ultima IV armour ladder: 8 tiers, defence 96 to 248, class constraints on the 144, 160, 176, 192, 208 tiers (conf/armors.xml lines 11-37)
DM armour types: wooden shield, armet, torso plate, leg plate, foot plate (engines/dm/dungeonman.h lines 179-185)
Xeen enchant types: element, attribute bonus, material, usable (engines/mm/xeen/item.h lines 55-59); six elements (lines 50-54)
zones: Ultima IV map kinds (conf/maps.xml): world 1, city 17 (castle 5, town 7, village 4, ruins 1 as city sub-types), combat 23, dungeon 8 (8 by 8, 8 levels; line 242), shrine 8
DM dungeon square types: wall, corridor, pit, stairs, door, teleporter, fake wall (engines/dm/dungeonman.h lines 47-62)

DM floor sensors: 9 types (party, creature, object, group generator, stairs, possession, version checker); wall sensors: 18 types including click ornaments, AND and OR gates, countdown walls (line 149), single and double projectile launchers, object exchanger, end game; champion portrait (127) (dungeonman.h lines 133-160)
Moongate: keyed to two moon phases; the destination is the gate for the second moon's phase (engines/ultima/ultima4/game/moongate.cpp lines 46-72)
Freescape: 3D areas with render depth layers and per-area condition code (engines/freescape/area.h); game data not read
Dungeon Master dungeon: a grid of squares with sensors (AU047)

looks.label: Effect tiles on ranged hits
looks.technique: Per-entry tile names for ranged hit and miss (magic flash, hit flash, fire field)

looks.label: Aura types
looks.technique: One aura per character, each with its own look: horn, jinx, negate, protection, quickness

looks.label: Projectile impact and explosion
looks.technique: Separate module for projectile and explosion effects, apart from melee

looks.label: Hazard body walking over others
looks.technique: Body moves onto other bodies and the party; fire-resistant

originals.name: Splitting Gel
originals.idea: A body that splits into a smaller body on a hit that does not kill it.
originals.change: Our split share, cooldown and look.

originals.name: Ember Field Hazard
originals.idea: A hazard body that walks over other bodies and burns what it touches.

originals.name: Leader Band
originals.idea: A band that follows one leader and attacks as one.
originals.change: Our band size and leader rules.

originals.name: Two-Clock Gate
originals.idea: A portal that opens only when two zone clocks agree.
originals.keep: Two cycles; destination set by the second clock (moongate.cpp line 61).

originals.name: Class-Gated Armour Ladder
originals.idea: A tier ladder where some classes cannot wear middle tiers.

originals.name: Returning Throw
originals.idea: A thrown weapon that comes back on a return arc.

originals.name: Timer Wall
originals.idea: A dungeon wall that opens on a timer after a trigger.

originals.name: Status Set as Icons
originals.idea: A fixed set of named afflictions, each with its own icon and sound.
